UnitStatement: The skills folder contains repo-native skills: reusable method packs that a bounded Type 2 agent may load at runtime.
Skills are not agents.
Skills do not have their own decision rights, write scopes, or interaction surfaces.
A skill method bundle tells an agent what task shape it is for.
A skill method bundle tells an agent which tools are preferred or allowed.
A skill method bundle tells an agent what runtime overrides matter.
A skill method bundle tells an agent what outputs should exist.
A skill method bundle tells an agent how to QA the run.
AGENT_TASK.md is the canonical loader for repo-native skills.
SKILLMAKER governs repo-native skills under the Type 0 standard AGENT_HELPS_HUMANS.md.
SKILLMAKER owns skill design, contract evolution, and subsystem governance.
Skill design outcomes conform to HELPS_HUMANS R10 + R12 and the "Design Outcomes for Skill Contracts" section.
A new skill is appropriate when the role stays the same.
A new skill is appropriate when write authority is supplied by the bounded TASK brief.
A new skill is appropriate when the interaction model stays the same.
A new skill is appropriate when the method and toolchain vary.
A different tool recipe for a bounded task is not sufficient reason to create a new agent.
When TASK loads a skill, human instructions in the run brief have highest precedence.
When TASK loads a skill, the TASK shell hard authorization boundary has second precedence.
When TASK loads a skill, the skill contract has third precedence.
When TASK loads a skill, skill defaults have fourth precedence.
A skill must never widen write authority beyond the TASK shell and effective bounded task brief.
When a persona agent dispatches TASK with TaskSkill, TASK automatically loads the skill's SKILL.md and companion files.
TASK automatic skill loading is the skill hydration guarantee.
The worker receives the full contract without the orchestrator reconstructing it in the dispatch prompt.
SKILL.md is the authoritative method and output contract for a skill.
BRIEF_SCHEMA.md is the dispatch contract for invoking a skill through TASK.
TOOL_POLICY.md defines the tool allowlist and preferences for a skill.
QA_CHECKS.md defines output validity checks for a skill.
The orchestrator provides runtime parameters via RuntimeOverrides.
The orchestrator may provide run-specific reinforcement via CustomInstructions.
The orchestrator does not duplicate the skill contract.
Each skill lives in its own folder under skills/.
Each skill folder requires SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter and Markdown body.
Each skill folder requires BRIEF_SCHEMA.md.
Each skill folder requires TOOL_POLICY.md.
Each skill folder requires QA_CHECKS.md.
A skill folder may include optional examples/.
A skill folder may include optional notes/.
A skill folder may include helper templates used by humans while drafting run briefs.
Every SKILL.md should state YAML frontmatter with at least name and description.
Every SKILL.md should state purpose and suitable task shapes.
Every SKILL.md should state required inputs.
Every SKILL.md should state optional runtime overrides.
Every SKILL.md should state output expectations.
Every SKILL.md should state whether the skill is safe for generic TASK.
Every SKILL.md should state important non-negotiable constraints.
SKILL.md frontmatter is the portable discovery surface.
The SKILL.md Markdown body is the Chirality execution guidance.
BRIEF_SCHEMA.md, TOOL_POLICY.md, and QA_CHECKS.md are required Chirality-specific companion files layered on top of SKILL.md.
Skills may reference deterministic tools under tools/ by policy, not by hidden assumption.
Good skill design makes preferred tools explicit.
Good skill design makes disallowed tools explicit.
Good skill design makes fallback conditions from tools to manual or LLM reasoning explicit.
Briefs and skills are orthogonal.
A brief supplies run-specific authority, scope inputs, write permissions, overrides, and expected outputs.
A skill supplies the method pack for a recurring task shape.
metadata.chirality-task-profile remains part of the repo metadata contract for compatibility.
metadata.chirality-task-profile should normally be NONE.
Non-NONE chirality-task-profile values are deprecated compatibility metadata, not write-scope grants.
deliverable-consistency should normally begin with tools/validation/scan_deliverable_consistency.py.
deliverable-consistency should read only flagged files and nearby context after scanning.
PDF2MD dispatches TASK + pdf2md-page for text transcription.
When ASSET_MODE is prose, PDF2MD dispatches TASK + pdf2md-page-assets for page-bounded figure, table, and image discovery.
PDF2MD deterministic tools materialize crops, CSVs, anchor page Markdown, aggregate the public asset manifest, and validate references.
DBM_PUBLISHER runs deterministic section mapping and section context packet generation before section dispatch.
DBM_PUBLISHER dispatches TASK + dbm-section-publish once per approved publication section with its read-only context packet.
DBM_PUBLISHER dispatches TASK + dbm-publish for package assembly, knowledge coverage/open-items records, and content adequacy.
TASK + dbm-postauthor-concordance builds a post-authoring evidence bundle using shared review-substrate tools and agent judgment.
The post-authoring evidence bundle prepares candidate findings for human disposition.
DBM_PUBLISHER may dispatch TASK + dbm-concordance-verify for semantic cross-section consistency observations.
All DBM publication skills remain publication-local and should be confined to _Publication/DBM/ scopes rather than mutating KTY-local truth.
WORKING_ITEMS dispatches TASK + dbm-draft-review to review a human-prepared draft DBM against the governed knowledge base.
dbm-draft-review runs deterministic substrate tools: scan_section_coverage.py, extract_claims.py, scan_tbd_markers.py, and check_body_thinness.py.
dbm-draft-review uses agent judgment to compare the substrate against governed truth.
dbm-draft-review prepares candidate findings for human disposition through the REVIEW agent.
dbm-concordance-seed is marked chirality-skill-status: LEGACY.
dbm-concordance-seed is no longer dispatched by DBM_PUBLISHER.
Concordance has moved from a pre-authoring gate to post-authoring evidence bundle review.
Agents should treat skills/ as a live skill root rather than relying on hard-coded skill lists in narrative documents.
Each immediate subfolder of skills/ that contains SKILL.md is treated as one repo-native skill.
Agents read skills/README.md first for the shared contract.
When a specific skill is requested, agents inspect that skill folder directly.
Specific skill inspection includes SKILL.md.
Specific skill inspection includes BRIEF_SCHEMA.md.
Specific skill inspection includes TOOL_POLICY.md.
Specific skill inspection includes QA_CHECKS.md.
Agents use the live skills/ folder rule for skill counts.
Agents use AGENTS.md and tools/REGISTRY.md for agent and tool indexes.
Agents must not assume any other document embedded skill list is current.
Agents must explicitly surface disagreement between live folder contents and a canonical index.
A well-bounded and auditable run invoked as TASK with a skill, scope, and tool permissions should probably be a skill, not a new top-level agent.
For new skills, the TaskSkill token should match the skill folder and name frontmatter exactly.
New skill names should prefer lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens only.
After adding or renaming skills, run python3 tools/validation/validate_skill_metadata.py skills.
validate_skill_metadata.py scans every immediate skill folder under skills/.
The validator validates skills/pdf2md/ and skills/deliverable-consistency/ using the same rules.
The validator checks the basic authoring contract: name, description, folder alignment, and required TOOL_POLICY.md presence.
The validator checks the machine-consumed runtime contract: metadata.chirality-*, canonical allowed-tools syntax, and tool-path resolution under tools/.
